_purpose: Declarative policy evaluated OUTSIDE the executing agent. This is deliberately NOT Rego and NOT OPA: NFR-12 keeps gates stdlib-only, CI installs only pytest, and a hand-written Rego interpreter would be a large dependency-shaped liability with no upside. What matters about policy-as-code is preserved -- the decision is computed from declared rules by a component the requester does not control, and returns a typed decision -- so the OPA DECISION INTERFACE is kept even though the language is not. If real OPA is adopted later, the interface does not change. POLICY_INTERFACE_PRESERVED != OPA_ADOPTED.
_default: Default is DENY. A request matching no rule is denied, never allowed: an unmatched request is an unclassified one, and the whole point of an external decision is that silence is not consent.

rules._note: No ticket, no work. Stated as its own rule so the denial names a cause.
An agent may not issue its own authority, whatever else is satisfied.

CONDITIONAL, never allow. Every mechanical precondition can hold and the merge still requires an authority this policy does not hold: at A3 merge is retained by the operator. A policy that could return allow here would be granting what it cannot.
A policy change cannot authorise its own adoption. Encoded as a rule so the refusal is computed rather than remembered.
